name: Apertus 1.5 Base (8B and 70B, long-context checkpoints)

lineage.family: Apertus 1.5 (SFT, DPO and RL instruct variants were published 2026-07-24 and 2026-08-22, before the sweep window and not recorded here)
lineage.how_derived: long-context-extended checkpoint of the pre-training pipeline (base model, no chat template)

purpose: Pre-training base models of the open Swiss national LLM family, for plain-text completion and as starting points for fine-tuning; separate SFT, RL and DPO repos cover instruction following and thinking mode (card via a page summarizer).

license.name: Apache-2.0 plus Acceptable Use Policy
license.notes: Tags and the card summary say Apache-2.0 with use also governed by an Acceptable Use Policy; files are gated behind a form sharing email and username with the authors, so no license text was read.

architecture.kind: dense transformer (details not on the visible card)
architecture.why_this_design: not stated on the visible card; the family card is summarized by a page summarizer only

pc-12gb.notes: no GGUF found; a base model is also not the target of Tona

engine_support.notes: Not checked beyond the card summary.

strengths: Fully open Swiss effort with an Apache-2.0 tag
Big gains over Apertus 1.0 (HumanEval 48.6 to 81.8, vendor)
weaknesses: Qwen3.5-9B scores higher on most reasoning, math and knowledge tasks in the card comparison
avoid_for: direct use as an assistant (base model)
soft.maturity: National research initiative; the 8B base has 3.2k downloads, the 70B base 86.

tona_fit.reason: Base checkpoints, gated, not stronger than the Qwen3.5 class in the vendor's own comparison; not a coding agent model. The RL instruct variants (earlier release) would be the ones to judge, outside this sweep.

sources.note: model card text read through a page summarizer (WebFetch); files gated, config and LICENSE not readable
metadata and sizes via the HF API

open_questions: Architecture, tokens trained and language list (card details not retrieved)
